video_caption: The video opens with an orange banner on a dark brown background, displaying the text "To convert the given galvanometer (of known resistance and figure of merit) into a voltmeter of a desired range and verify the same." The "Blueprint EDUCATION" logo is in the top-left corner, and a smaller version of the objective text is at the top-right. The scene then transitions to a classroom or laboratory setting with two animated female characters. The character on the left wears a white lab coat and a pink scarf, standing with her hands clasped, smiling, while the character on the right wears a dark blazer, red tie, and white headband, holding a red book and smiling. In the background, there's a blackboard, a "Blueprint !" poster, a Newton's cradle, an hourglass, a lab stand with a flask, and blue lab benches. A speech bubble appears next to the woman in the lab coat, stating, "Galvanometer is a sensitive device used to detect very low current. Its working is based on the principle that a coil placed in a uniform magnetic field experiences a torque when an electric current is set up in it." Following this, the girl with the red book asks, "How can we convert the given galvanometer (of known resistance and figure of merit) into a voltmeter of a desired range and verify the same?" The copyright text "© Blueprint Education All Rights Reserved" remains visible at the bottom of the screen throughout.

In a vibrant green laboratory setting with blue cabinets and scientific instruments on the counters, two animated female figures are present. On the left, a woman in a white dress and a pink scarf gestures with both hands as if explaining something. On the right, a younger girl in a black blazer, white shirt, and red tie stands, holding a red book, and smiles. Above them, a banner displays "BLUEPRINT EDUCATION" and the objective: "TO CONVERT THE GIVEN GALVANOMETER INTO A VOLTMETER OF A DESIRED RANGE AND VERIFY THE SAME." A light blue elliptical speech bubble appears on the right side, stating: "A galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter of desired range by connecting a suitable high resistance R in its series." In the background, a framed image of a horseshoe magnet with glowing magnetic field lines hangs on the wall.

At the start of the segment, two animated female characters are positioned in a laboratory setting. On the left, an adult woman in a white lab coat and pink scarf stands, speaking with animated mouth movements. To her right, a younger girl in a black blazer and white top holds a book and looks attentively at the woman. Between them, a large green oval prominently displays the formula "R = V / Ig - G". In the top right, a banner reads: "TO CONVERT THE GIVEN GALVANOMETER INTO A VOLTMETER OF A DESIRED RANGE AND VERIFY THE SAME." (Meaning: The objective is to transform a given galvanometer into a voltmeter of a specific range and then confirm its accuracy). The background features various lab equipment such as a Newton's Cradle, an hourglass, and other apparatus on a workbench. The "Blueprint EDUCATION" logo is visible in the top left, and "© Blueprint Education All Rights Reserved." is at the bottom of the screen. As the segment progresses, the adult woman gestures slightly with her right hand, and the formula oval remains on screen.

The video segment displays an animated physics laboratory setup on a brown tabletop against a dark teal background. Various electrical components are connected by wires, including a white battery, a black key switch, a black meter (likely an ammeter), a light yellow galvanometer with a circular display and a needle pointing to 'G' at its center, a large cylindrical rheostat, and a beige resistance box with several key plugs. A blue banner at the top reads "Blueprint EDUCATION" on the left and "TO CONVERT THE GIVEN GALVANOMETER INTO A VOLTMETER OF A DESIRED RANGE AND VERIFY THE SAME." on the right, indicating the experiment's objective. An orange box on the bottom left states "Procedure," and a white text box on the right outlines step "2. Note the total number of divisions (n) on either side of the zero of the galvanometer." The galvanometer is slightly zoomed in, showing its dial markings and the 'G' symbol. A blue bar at the bottom displays "© Blueprint Education All Rights Reserved." The scene remains static throughout the segment, with the text as the only changing element from the previous step.

The video opens with an animated circuit diagram displayed on a teal background. At the top left, the "Blueprint EDUCATION" logo is visible. A banner across the top states: "TO CONVERT THE GIVEN GALVANOMETER INTO A VOLTMETER OF A DESIRED RANGE AND VERIFY THE SAME." The circuit diagram includes a battery, a key labeled "K," a rheostat labeled "Rheostat (Potential divider)," a voltmeter (indicated by a "V" in a circle), and a galvanometer (indicated by a "G" in a circle) connected in series with a resistance box labeled "R HRB" within a dashed box. The galvanometer and resistance box, representing the converted voltmeter, are connected in parallel with a portion of the rheostat, which is connected in series with the battery and key. An orange banner at the bottom left reads "Procedure," and a larger orange box on the right displays the instruction: "B. Verification of the converted voltmeter: 6. Draw a neat circuit diagram for the verification of the converted voltmeter." The bottom of the screen shows the copyright text: "© Blueprint Education All Rights Reserved."

In a vibrant blue laboratory setting, a woman with brown hair, dressed in a white lab coat and pink scarf, stands on the left, gesturing with both hands as if explaining something. To her right, a young girl in a black blazer and red tie smiles, attentively listening. Behind them, on a blue counter, various lab equipment is arranged, including a balance scale, a Newton's cradle, an hourglass, a stand with a clamp, and a wooden box, with a ruler laid out across the counter. A framed picture depicting magnetic field lines hangs on the wall. At the top of the screen, a "Blueprint EDUCATION" logo is visible alongside the objective text: "TO CONVERT THE GIVEN GALVANOMETER INTO A VOLTMETER OF A DESIRED RANGE AND VERIFY THE SAME." An orange banner in the foreground displays "Observations" in white, below which four lines of text appear sequentially as the woman speaks: "1. Given resistance of the galvanometer (G) = X ....... ohm." (Given resistance of the galvanometer (G) = X ....... ohm.), "2. Given value of the figure of merit of the galvanometer (K) = A/division." (Given value of the figure of merit of the galvanometer (K) = A/division.), "3. Total number of divisions on either side of the zero of the galvanometer (n) = X ....... divisions." (Total number of divisions on either side of the zero of the galvanometer (n) = X ....... divisions.), and "4. Current for full scale deflection (Ig) = nK = X ....... amp." (Current for full scale deflection (Ig) = nK = X ....... amp.).

The video segment opens in a blue-green lab setting with two female animated characters: a woman in a white lab coat and pink scarf standing on the left, and a younger woman in a black blazer and red tie sitting at a desk on the right, smiling. The woman in the lab coat stands upright, facing forward, and occasionally makes gentle hand gestures as text appears. The upper banner displays "Blueprint Education" and text stating, "TO CONVERT THE GIVEN GALVANOMETER INTO A VOLTMETER OF A DESIRED RANGE AND VERIFY THE SAME." (to convert the given galvanometer into a voltmeter of a desired range and verify the same). The bottom left corner shows "Blueprint Lab." A series of "Observations" text boxes appear sequentially at the bottom of the screen, each displaying a numbered point with a formula and a blank 'x' for a value, which a female voice reads aloud. First, "5. Range of conversion of the converted voltmeter (V) = x ohm." (The 'x' represents a numerical value for the range of conversion of the converted voltmeter in ohms). Then, "6. Value of the required series resistance (R) = V/Ig - G = x ohm." (The 'x' represents a numerical value for the required series resistance in ohms, calculated using the given formula). Next, "7. Least count of the converted voltmeter V/n = x volt." (The 'x' represents a numerical value for the least count of the converted voltmeter in volts, calculated using the given formula). Finally, "8. Least count of the standard voltmeter = x volt." (The 'x' represents a numerical value for the least count of the standard voltmeter in volts). At 00:29, the scene transitions to a full-screen table titled "Table for the verification of converted voltmeter," with columns for "S.No.", "Reading of converted voltmeter" (subdivided into "Deflection θ (division)" and "Potential difference V₁ = θ x L.C. (volt)"), "Standard voltmeter reading V₂ (volt)", and "Difference (Error) V₂ - V₁ (volt)". The "Observations" label remains at the bottom left.

The video segment opens with a static image of a light blue table titled "Table for the verification of converted voltmeter." (volt)"), "Standard voltmeter reading V₂ (volt)", and "Difference (Error) V₂ - V₁ (volt)". All four rows beneath the headers are empty. An orange banner at the bottom left of the screen displays "Observations," and a blue footer reads "© Blueprint Education All Rights Reserved." (English translation: "Blueprint Education All Rights Reserved."). A female voice reads out the table's column headers. At 00:03, the scene transitions to an animated laboratory setting where two women are present. On the left, a light-skinned woman with brown hair tied back, wearing a white lab coat over a light blue top with a pink scarf, stands with her hands clasped and a neutral expression. On the right, a light-skinned woman with dark hair in a bun, wearing a dark blue blazer, a white shirt, and a red tie, is seated at a wooden lab bench, facing left with a gentle smile and her eyes closed. The laboratory background includes various scientific instruments like a Newton's cradle, beakers, an hourglass, and a ruler. A "Blueprint Lab" logo is visible in the top left corner, and the orange banner at the bottom now displays "Result."

The video segment displays an animated scene set in a laboratory or classroom, featuring a blue-teal wall and a light brown wooden desk with scientific equipment. On the left side of the screen, a woman with light brown hair tied back, wearing a white lab coat and a pink/purple scarf, stands and gestures with open hands as she speaks. On the right, a girl with dark brown hair in a bun and a white headband, dressed in a dark suit jacket with a red tie and white shirt, sits at the desk, smiling and looking towards the woman. In the background, an hourglass, a Newton's cradle, and other lab equipment are visible on the desk, and a framed picture depicting abstract blue and purple shapes hangs on the wall. A "Blueprint EDUCATION" logo and the text "TO CONVERT THE GIVEN GALVANOMETER INTO A VOLTMETER OF A DESIRED RANGE AND VERIFY THE SAME." (to convert the given galvanometer into a voltmeter of a desired range and verify the same) are displayed in a banner at the top, indicating the purpose of the virtual experiment. A "Blueprint Lab" logo is also present on the left. An orange "Result" box on the left side of the screen sequentially displays three points:
1.  "The value of the required series resistance to be connected in series with the galvanometer to convert it into voltmeter of the given range = ......x ohm." (This describes the calculated series resistance needed to convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter for a specific voltage range).
2.  "Value of the current for full scale deflection, Ig = ..........x amp." (This refers to the current at which the galvanometer shows maximum deflection).
3.  "The difference between the values of standard voltmeter and converted voltmeter, i.e. (V2 – V1) is very small, hence, conversion of the given galvanometer into voltmeter of the given range is perfect." (This concludes that the conversion of the galvanometer to a voltmeter was successful due to minimal difference between its reading and a standard voltmeter).
The woman continues to speak and gesture, while the girl maintains a smiling, attentive expression as the result texts appear. A bottom banner reads "© Blueprint Education All Rights Reserved."
